prompt: Each fission of a uranium-235 nucleus releases about 200 MeV. Estimate the energy released by fission of 1.0 kg of uranium-235 and compare it with burning 1.0 kg of coal (about 30 MJ). (1 MeV $=1.6\times10^{-13}$ J, 1 u $=1.66\times10^{-27}$ kg)
markscheme:
Nuclei in 1 kg $=\dfrac{1.0}{235\times1.66\times10^{-27}}=2.6\times10^{24}$ **(A1)**

$E=2.6\times10^{24}\times200\times1.6\times10^{-13}=8.2\times10^{13}$ J **(A1)**; about $3\times10^{6}$ times more than coal **(A1)**

prompt: Explain how a chain reaction is sustained in a nuclear reactor, and what 'critical' means.
markscheme: Each fission releases 2–3 neutrons, which can cause further fissions **(R1)**; critical: on average exactly one neutron from each fission causes another, so the rate is steady **(R1)**

concept: Components of a nuclear power plant
prompt: State the function of **(a)** the moderator, **(b)** the control rods, **(c)** the heat exchanger and **(d)** the shielding in a nuclear power station.
markscheme:
**(a)** Slows fast neutrons by collisions so they are more likely to cause fission **(A1)**

**(b)** Absorb neutrons; inserted further to reduce the reaction rate **(A1)**

**(c)** Transfers thermal energy from the coolant to water, producing steam for the turbines **(A1)**

**(d)** Absorbs radiation (neutrons and gamma) to protect workers **(A1)**

prompt: Explain why fission products are dangerous and describe how high-level waste is managed.
markscheme: Fission products are neutron-rich and highly radioactive, some with long half-lives **(R1)**; spent fuel is cooled in water ponds, then vitrified and stored in sealed containers deep underground, isolated for thousands of years **(A1)**
